newsitem.title: UK: Consumers to hold building society windfalls.
newsitem.headline: Consumers to hold building society windfalls.

text.p: Over half of UK consumers receiving windfalls from demutualised building societies will hold on to the shares, according to a survey.

Gavin Anderson & Company, in a survey of unit trust investors, found 56 percent of windfall share recipients planning to hold them, while 22 percent will transfer them to personal equity plans (PEPs).
Only eight percent will sell some or all their shares for specific personal expenditure and a further seven percent will sell some or all for further savings and investments.

"Despite expectations that windfalls will fuel consumer spending, our findings indicate that few investors will be cashing in their new shares for their own personal expenditure, e.g. holidays," said James White of Gavin Anderson.
Up to 35 billion stg of shares have been distributed by the demutualised building societies.
In total, 62 percent of all unit trust investors questioned will receive some windfall shares as a result of building society demutualisations.
Of windfall share holders planning to reinvest their shares, 78 percent will invest in PEPs, while nine percent will invest in equities and six percent in building society accounts.

The survey also found that 66 percent of consumers are optimistic for the future prospects of unit trusts, a nine percent increase from six months ago and the highest figure recorded since November 1993.
The most common reason cited for optimism was confidence in the government, expressed by 31 percent, while 23 percent cited a recovering economy.
The survey consisted of a sample of 600 unit trust and unit trust-based PEP investors, and was conducted between May 6 and May 30.
